items.performers: Philip Glass Ensemble, Michael Riesman, conductor; Paul Zukofsky, violin
items.recorded: Big Apple Recording Studios, New York, 1978
items.label: Tomato; CBS Masterworks (now Sony Classical)
items.note: The first recording of the opera, abridged by Glass to four LPs, with Zukofsky as the violinist in the part dressed as Einstein. Glass’s sleeve note says that the most important musical material appears in the knee plays and features the violin.

items.performers: Philip Glass Ensemble; Michael Riesman, conductor; Philip Glass, electric organ
items.label: CBS Masterworks (now Sony Classical)
items.note: Six pieces written for the recording studio. In the published score Opening is for solo piano and Façades for two soprano saxophones, viola and cello, with an optional synthesizer. Glass’s note says the music was meant to introduce his work to a more general audience.

items.performers: Stuttgart State Opera Orchestra and Chorus, Dennis Russell Davies; Paul Esswood (Akhnaten), Milagro Vargas (Nefertiti)
items.recorded: Karlshöhe Church and Tonstudio Bauer, Ludwigsburg
items.label: Sony Classical
items.note: Recorded with the company and conductor of the 1984 first performance. Glass made a complete synthesizer recording of the opera in real time and sent the tapes to the Stuttgart production team eight months before the opening. Texts from the Amarna period are sung in their original languages and the orchestra has no violins.

items.performers: Kronos Quartet (David Harrington, John Sherba, Hank Dutt, Joan Jeanrenaud)
items.label: Nonesuch
items.note: The album plays the quartets in the order 5, 4, 2, 3. No. 5 was written for the Kronos Quartet, No. 2 (“Company”) for a staging of Beckett’s prose poem, and No. 3 takes its six movements from the music Glass wrote for Paul Schrader’s film Mishima. The album was released in 1995.
